episodic_copy.task: unseen WordNet lemma identity with two corrupted characters; emit first 24 bytes of stored gloss
episodic_copy.interpretation: exact retrieval-and-copy of stored text, not independent generation

native_root_episodic.interpretation: gauge-invariant triangle transport preserves the selected 24-byte record; conventional indexed copy has identical selection accuracy

non_claims: This is not a fluent language model; free-form samples remain incoherent.
The episodic decoder hard-copies an already stored 24-byte answer; it does not synthesize unseen prose.
A conventional indexed copy system obtains identical 118/120 selection accuracy.
The cycle geometry has no demonstrated predictive gain in the matched byte-LM comparison.
The native episodic experiment is C++ over ordinary RAM, not NaN16 native execution or quantum hardware.
The episode root is re-instantiated per test; allocation costs are excluded from inference claims.
The gauge shift is a controlled classical reference-frame change, not a general robustness proof.
No canonical merge or live deployment is claimed.

integration.next_gate: jointly train a copy gate with the byte LM and compare against matched attention memory on held-out bits-per-byte, exact facts, latency, and memory
